pr_title: Fix nullref when getting struct from feature collection and it isn't present
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/46939

I believe `if (typeof(TFeature).IsValueType)` is intrinsic which should mean the JIT will optimize this like crazy and be a noop in the common class case. Did a quick microbenchmark to check and it showed no difference.
pr_comments:
Random thought, what happens if someone asks for a struct, but the struct is nullable?

```cs
var i = context.Features.Get<int?>();
```
Is that saying:
1. Give me the type registered as `int?`, but if it isn't registered then error. Or,
2. Give me the type registered as `int`, but if it isn't registered then return `int?` with a value of null.

I'm guessing 1 is what we have at the moment and what we probably want. Anything else is too fancy/confusing/unnecessary.

```cs
var isStructRegistered = context.Features[typeof(int)] is not null;
```
For checking if a struct value is present, I think the code above works.

> Give me the type registered as int?, but if it isn't registered then error

Almost, it returns null if it isn't registered because we can return a null struct then. It only errors if you use a non-nullable struct and it's not registered.

> var isStructRegistered = context.Features[typeof(int)] is not null;
For checking if a struct value is present, I think the code above works.

I don't understand what you're trying to say.

I thinking out loud if there is a way for someone to check if a struct feature is registered. The usual pattern of `context.Feature.Get<IMyFeature>() is not null` won't work. They need to use the `Type` indexer. It returns the feature typed as an object, but it was probably already typed as an object when stored by the feature collection.

> Also, this would required a breaking change notice for the new behavior, yes?

The only change is a NullReferenceException is now an InvalidOperationException (in an obscure scenario IMO). I don't think that warrants a breaking change notification?

issue_context.title: FeatureCollection can throw NRE with structs
issue_context.body:
This code is not supposed to throw an exception but return `null`. However, when the type is a struct then it will throw an NRE.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6647d80ab886b8616e5b34812853e00358c93ce5/src/Extensions/Features/src/FeatureCollection.cs#L118-L121

The compiler calls [UnBox](https://source.dot.net/#System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/CompilerServices/CastHelpers.cs,525) which shouldn't be invoked with a `null` object.

Should the type have the `class` constraint? 
Should this case be handled? 
An analyzer limitation?
comments: Triage: we should check if TFeature is a struct type and if it's null, just return default (don't try to unbox it).

> check if TFeature is a struct type and if it's null, just return default

We shouldn't return `default` for struct types, that would break user assumptions that the feature is present. Instead we should return null when using `Get<TFeature?>` and throw an `InvalidOperationException` for `Get<TFeature>` when the result is null, instead of the current NRE.

review_comments: Feels a little weird that `int` and `int?` are stored separately, but I assume it doesn't matter in practice.

The key is the type in the feature collection.

We could unwrap `Nullable<T>` on get/set, but no one has asked for it, and it feels like something that is a little too clever that will cause unanticipated problems later.
